newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton rises, bad weather hits arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton rises, bad weather hits arrivals.

text.p: Cotton prices rose on Thursday helped by fresh demand and lower arrivals hit by bad weather in northern India, traders said.
They said the Cotton Corporation of India was a buyer.
Arrivals in the Punjab region dropped to 20,000 bales (170 kg each) against 25,000 bales due to severe cold weather.
In the spot deals Punjab saw-ginned moved up 10 rupees to 1,460/1,650 per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi looked up 5.0 rupees to 840/875 per maund.
Gujarat cotton was quiet in limited activity with Gujarat Sankar-4 steady at 18,000/18,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
